title: The Truth About Lab-Grown Diamonds
body_text:
Still wondering if lab-grown diamonds are the real deal?

I keep finding myself comparing where I am now to where I was a year ago all the time. And if there’s a silver lining in everything that’s happened, it’s that I don’t think I would have appreciated the little things quite this much before. A dinner. Getting dressed up. Feeling good. Celebrating another year together. Things that might have once felt ordinary suddenly feel like everything.

I am so excited to get dressed up in @bluenilediamond for the evening and celebrate this milestone in pieces that feel just as meaningful as the moment itself. A sparkling cocktail for an iconic collection✨@brilliantearth #AD

This sparkling amethyst cocktail is inspired by @brilliantearth’s stunning Elizabeth Taylor Collection!

The Elizabeth Taylor Champagne Cocktail 🍾✨
1.5 oz gin
1 oz creme de violette
.5 oz lemon juice, fresh
Top with champagne or prosecco
Garnish: lemon twist

Method: combine all ingredients except champagne/prosecco in a cocktail shaker with ice and shake until chilled. Fine strain into a chilled coupe or martini glass. Top with bubbles. Garnish with a lemon twist (and a pearl spoon of caviar, if you’re feeling extra) ✨

Cheers!

Our first anniversary came around the same time I was diagnosed with cancer. We had this beautiful trip planned that our wedding planner had organized for us, and we ended up canceling it. Our second anniversary, I was deep in treatment and too sick to really celebrate.

I keep finding myself comparing where I am now to where I was a year ago all the time. And if there’s a silver lining in everything that’s happened, it’s that I don’t think I would have appreciated the little things quite this much before. A dinner. Getting dressed up. Feeling good. Celebrating another year together. Things that might have once felt ordinary suddenly feel like everything.

I am so excited to get dressed up in @bluenilediamond for the evening and celebrate this milestone in pieces that feel just as meaningful as the moment itself. I love that these natural diamond essentials can be worn for dressy occasions, but are are just as beautiful incorporated into my everyday. #BlueNilePartner

THE NEW INDIA
THE MODERN INTER-CULTURAL WEDDING DRESS CODE
 
In an age of noise, Sabyasachi chooses silence, intention over conformity, and substance over spectacle.
This is not bridal wear for performance. It’s a refusal to conform. It ignores trends and refutes that tradition must be loud to be appreciated.
Lehengas, rich with craft, are paired with quiet dupattas so the embroidery can breathe. The styling is spare; jewellery edited; every detail essential. She chooses with discernment and wears heritage as presence, not performance.
In the New India, maximalism and minimalism meet like memory and intention. A balance. A tightrope above the stereotypical. As brides declare for themselves who they are; when they seek truth over validation, they become a catalyst for change. As Sabyasachi has always said: “For heritage to be relevant, it must be dynamic.”

THE NEW WORLD
THE MODERN MULTICULTURAL WEDDING DRESS CODE
 
In love, everything becomes ancestral. This collection is about heritage in motion.
 
As more Indian men and women find love across continents, cultures, and genders, I find myself drawn to the quiet transformations taking place inside weddings. Cross-cultural unions are entering Indian tradition with humility.
 
“The New World” is my response to this moment: a bridal collection that leans into traditional silhouettes but is stripped of excess. The jewellery is edited, deliberate. The fabrics are still opulent, but the styling is more nuanced. The dupattas are lighter, sometimes even translucent. There is a dignity in their weightlessness.
 
This is not a dilution of culture; it is refinement. For these couples, their choices speak of initiation, not appropriation, presence over performance. Occidental preference to edit has found harmony with the oriental instinct to ornament. This is India; not inherited but chosen, which is the most modern act of all.

She fell in love with everything.
The first sip of chai in the morning. Rain tapping against the window. Books with folded corners. People who laughed with their whole heart.
Every time something made her smile, a tiny red heart appeared on her.
One became two. Two became twenty.
Soon, she was covered in little reminders that love isn’t rare at all. It’s everywhere, if you remember to notice it.
That’s how she became Safed Ishq.
Soft as a blank page, carrying tiny embroidered hearts like secrets only the observant can find. She doesn’t believe love needs a reason. She simply believes there’s always room for one more little heart.

Love doesn’t always arrive with grand gestures. Sometimes, it lingers in little moments, a shared smile, a handwritten note, or a heart doodled in the corner of a page. Safed Ishq celebrates exactly that. Crafted from Suta’s signature feather-soft mul cotton in a serene white, this borderless saree is scattered with tiny embroidered red hearts, adding a playful touch to an otherwise understated drape. Light, breathable, and full of charm, it’s a saree that wears its heart with quiet confidence.

(Suta, Suta Bombay, Suta Saree, Suta Blouse, Suta New, New Launch, Shop Now, Priya Malik)

Our Kalo Jam blouse looks innocent. All black, sitting quietly in the wardrobe, minding her own business. Until you discover the sleeves.
One side? Pretty black butti.
Flip.
Suddenly, black brocade.
Because apparently, Kalo Jam has a secret side. Or two. She’s the kind of blouse that gets bored easily, so she keeps her options open. A little zari here, a little brocade there, and a quick sleeve flip when she feels like changing things up.
Sweet name. Dark mood. Double personality. Kalo Jam doesn’t ask, “Which look are we wearing tonight?” She says, “Why choose?”

(Suta, Suta Bombay, Suta New, Suta Saree, Shop Now, New Launch, Agomoni, Suta Blouse)

She always arrived with the rain.
Not the loud kind that rushed through the streets, but the gentle drizzle that made people pause by their windows. She loved the hush that came before the first drop, the smell of wet earth, and the way the whole world seemed to slow down for a while.
As she walked, tiny silver raindrops settled on her, refusing to leave. They sparkled with every step, as if the rain wanted to stay close a little longer.
That’s why they called her Saawan.
She carries the monsoon with her, not in thunder or storms, but in quiet showers that soothe the soul. Wrap her around yourself, and you’ll hear the soft rhythm of rain, reminding you that sometimes, the gentlest moments leave the deepest imprint.

Like rain meeting still waters, Saawan is calm, refreshing, and quietly enchanting. Crafted from Suta’s signature feather-soft mul cotton in a soothing teal, this borderless saree is sprinkled with delicate silver sequins that shimmer like raindrops caught in the light. Light, breathable, and effortlessly graceful, it’s made for days when you want to carry the magic of the monsoon wherever you go.

Our Kalo Jam blouse looks innocent. All black, sitting quietly in the wardrobe, minding her own business. Until you discover the sleeves.
One side? Pretty black butti.
Flip.
Suddenly, black brocade.
Because apparently, Kalo Jam has a secret side. Or two. She’s the kind of blouse that gets bored easily, so she keeps her options open. A little zari here, a little brocade there, and a quick sleeve flip when she feels like changing things up.
Sweet name. Dark mood. Double personality. Kalo Jam doesn’t ask, “Which look are we wearing tonight?” She says, “Why choose?”
